item.title: 1972: The New York Yankees Acquire Third Baseman Graig Nettles
item.description: The New York Yankees acquire third baseman Graig Nettles, who will be a cornerstone of their 1977 and 1978 World Series championship teams—and a five-time American League All-Star and 2x Gold Glove Award-winner over 11 seasons in New York—when the Cleveland Indians swap Nettles and catcher Jerry Moses to the Yankees for catcher John Ellis, infielder Jerry Kenney, and outfielders Charlie Spikes and Rusty Torres. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 2024: The Miami Marlins Hired Moskos to Be the Team's Major League Pitching
item.description: On November 27, 2024, the Miami Marlins hired Moskos to be the team's major league pitching coach.

item.title: 2023: Castillo Signed a Minor League Contract With the Arizona Diamondbacks
item.description: On November 27, 2023, Castillo signed a minor league contract with the Arizona Diamondbacks. Photo: luvsd on Flickr (Original version) 佾珜 (Crop) (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2022: Brown Was Hired to Be the Hitting Coach for the Miami Marlins
item.description: On November 27, 2022, Brown was hired to be the hitting coach for the Miami Marlins.

item.title: 2020: Subero Was Announced as the New Manager for the Hanwha Eagles
item.description: On November 27, 2020, Subero was announced as the new manager for the Hanwha Eagles of the KBO League. Photo: Joel Dinda (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2019: The Pittsburgh Pirates Name Derek Shelton
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates name Derek Shelton as the team's new manager replacing Clint Hurdle who was fired at the end of the previous season and he later retired from Managing this is Derek Shelton's first Major League Managerial job. Photo: Keith Allison (CC BY-SA 2.0).

item.title: 2013: As of November 27, 2013, According to The Washington Post
item.description: As of November 27, 2013, according to The Washington Post, it appeared that only minor work had been done on the One Loudoun site, but there was nothing which looked like the beginning of a baseball stadium.

item.title: 2012: It Was Announced Somerset's Pitching Coach
item.description: On November 27, 2012, it was announced Somerset's pitching coach and former major league pitcher, Brett Jodie, would become the new manager with Lyle becoming manager emeritus. Photo: Jeffrey Hayes (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 2001: The Major League Owners Vote Unanimously to Extend Baseball
item.description: The major league owners vote unanimously to extend baseball commissioner Bud Selig's contract through 2006. Photo: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff on Flickr (Original version) (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1997: Buck Leonard, 90, Hall of Fame First Baseman Who Played in Negro
item.description: Buck Leonard, 90, Hall of Fame first baseman who played in Negro league baseball from 1934 through 1950 with the Homestead Grays, helping them to win three Negro World Series championships and earning 13 All-Star selections, while ranking regularly among the league leaders in batting average and home runs. Photo: Library of Congress (Public domain).

item.title: 1985: Vince Coleman, Who Stole 110 Bases for the St. Louis Cardinals Last
item.description: Vince Coleman, who stole 110 bases for the St. Louis Cardinals last season, third highest in the modern era, joins Frank Robinson (1956), Orlando Cepeda (1958) and Willie McCovey (1959) as the only unanimous winners of the NL Rookie of the Year Award. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1984: The American League Gold Glove Team Is Announced
item.description: The American League Gold Glove team is announced, and is made up of the same nine players as the 1983 team: Ron Guidry (P), Lance Parrish (C), Eddie Murray (1B), Lou Whitaker (2B), Buddy Bell (3B), Alan Trammell (SS), Dwight Evans (OF), Dave Winfield (OF) and Dwayne Murphy (OF). Photo: oaktree_brian_1976 (CC BY 2.0).

item.title: 1981: In a Swap of AL All-Star Outfielders
item.description: In a swap of AL All-Star outfielders, the Detroit Tigers send left-handed-swinging Steve Kemp to the Chicago White Sox for the right-handed Chet Lemon. Photo: User Phil5329 on en.wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1973: San Francisco Giants Left Fielder Gary Matthews, Who Hit .300
item.description: San Francisco Giants left fielder Gary Matthews, who hit .300 with 12 home runs and 58 RBI in 145 games, outpolls eight others receiving 11 of 24 nominations for the National League Rookie of the Year Award. The runners-up are Steve Rogers (P), Bob Boone (C), Dan Driessen (3B), Elías Sosa (P), Ron Cey (3B), Johnny Grubb (CF), Davey Lopes (2B) and Richie Zisk (RF). Photo: Dealphungo (CC BY-SA 3.0).

item.title: 1970: Pitcher Carl Morton, Who Posted an 18–11 Record
item.description: Pitcher Carl Morton, who posted an 18–11 record with 154 strikeouts and a 3.60 ERA for the last-place Montreal Expos, receives the National League Rookie of the Year Award. Morton beats out Cincinnati Reds outfielder Bernie Carbo, who hit .310 with 21 home runs and 63 RBI.

item.title: 1967: The New York Mets Trade Pitcher Bill Denehy
item.description: The New York Mets trade pitcher Bill Denehy and $100,000 to the Washington Senators for Washington's ex-manager, Gil Hodges, who on October 11 became the third permanent skipper in the Mets' seven-year history. The former Brooklyn Dodgers great and eventual Hall of Famer will lead the 1969 "Miracle Mets" to the world championship. Photo: Wikimedia Commons (Public domain).

item.title: 1958: Harry G. Salsinger, 71, Sportswriter for the Detroit News for Over 50
item.description: Harry G. Salsinger, 71, sportswriter for the Detroit News for over 50 years.

item.title: 1953: Cleveland Indians Third Baseman Al Rosen
item.description: Cleveland Indians third baseman Al Rosen, who missed out on the American League's Triple Crown by .0015 batting average points, is unanimously selected the AL's Most Valuable Player. Photo: Bowman Gum (Public domain).

item.title: 1947: Triple Crown Winner Ted Williams (.343 BA, 32 Home Runs
item.description: Triple Crown winner Ted Williams (.343 BA, 32 home runs, 114 RBI) of the Boston Red Sox is edged out by Joe DiMaggio (.315, 20, 97) for the American League MVP Award by one point. Controversy erupts when it's reported that one BBWAA member has failed to include Williams anywhere on his ballot. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1943: Bill Veeck, the 29-Year-Old "Maverick" Co-Owner of the Milwaukee
item.description: Bill Veeck, the 29-year-old "maverick" co-owner of the Milwaukee Brewers of the American Association, enlists in the United States Marines as a private. A relentless, creative baseball promoter, Veeck has built the Brewers into a success on the field and at the turnstiles. Photo: US Marine Corps (Public domain).

item.title: 1922: Austin McHenry, 27, Dies From a Brain Tumor After Hitting .350
item.description: Austin McHenry, 27, dies from a brain tumor after hitting .350 with 17 home runs and 110 RBI for the 1921 St. Louis Cardinals, who became ill during the 1922 season and was hitting .303 when forced to quit. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).

item.title: 1912: Fred Corey, 57[?], 3B/P/OF Who Posted a 27–46 Record
item.description: Fred Corey, 57[?], 3B/P/OF who posted a 27–46 record and hit a .246 average for the Providence Grays, Worcester Ruby Legs and Philadelphia Athletics between 1878 and 1885. Photo: Unknown author (Public domain).
